title: A-PSRO: A Unified Strategy Learning Method with Advantage Metric for Normal-form Games
authors: Yudong Hu; Haoran Li; Congying Han; Tiande Guo; Bonan Li; Mingqiang Li
independent_acceptance: focused scientific check completed; scientific adjudication pending

problems.title: Theorem4.2 pure-direction improvement is false
problems.evidence: Explicit antisymmetric4x4 matrix, interior theta singleton meta-equilibrium, Vtheta=-3/4; all pure directions strictly worsen V for every0<d<=1 while mixed direction improves. Full formulas and exact calculations in report/check program.
problems.counterreading: Diversity/random population expansion may escape; no claim full stochastic method never converges.
problems.repair_status: Mixed-direction repair candidate locally verified; replacement algorithm/rate not established

independent_check.original_and_assumptions: Read p2 definitions separating pure-action set A from mixed-strategy simplex, p4 Theorem4.2, AppendixA.5 pp15-16 and Algorithm2 p20. Population members are mixed strategies; a singleton interior theta is an admissible meta-game action, and its single zero-payoff restricted game is trivially an equilibrium.
independent_check.independent_derivation: Verified antisymmetry and theta positivity/sum1. Fresh Fraction arithmetic gives theta^T A=(1/4,-3/4,-3/4,-3/4). For e1 the active columns remain-3/4-d/4; for each other pure action its -2 payoff column yields-3/4-5d/4 and is no larger than the other columns for0<d<=1. At d=1/100 fresh values are(-301/400,-61/80,-61/80,-61/80); at d=1e-6 they are(-3000001/4000000,-600001/800000,-600001/800000,-600001/800000). Mixed m=(0,1/3,1/3,1/3) has m^T A=(1,0,0,0), yielding genuine improvement3d/4.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_scope: Concavity permits an improving mixture without improving any vertex direction at a nonsmooth point. AppendixA.5 positive-inner-product step does not imply Eq19. Random/diversity/population expansion branches in Algorithm2 can escape, so no full-algorithm nonconvergence claim follows.
independent_check.severity_and_repair: Major retained: universal deterministic pure-direction guarantee and its claimed sublinear consequence fail under all stated conditions. Allowing a mixed improving oracle restores the segment inequality but changes the algorithm and gives no verified rate.

problems.title: Theorem4.6 optimistic advantage is discontinuous in a simplified game
problems.evidence: A=diag(2,1), B=diag(1,2); no dominated actions. At row p=2/3 optimistic V jumps from1/3 to4/3. Exact rational ratios diverge.
problems.counterreading: Strict-best-response regions are locally linear; that does not imply global Lipschitzness.
problems.repair_status: No global repair established under current assumptions

independent_check.original_and_assumptions: Read p5 Definitions4.3/4.5 and Theorem4.6, and p16 AppendixA.7. For A=diag(2,1),B=diag(1,2), every pure action is strictly best against some opponent pure action, so the unusually quantified dominated-action definition removes none.
independent_check.independent_derivation: Against row p, column payoffs are p and2-2p. Below2/3 the chosen column is2 and row reward1-p; above it column1 gives2p. At equality optimistic tie-breaking picks4/3 rather than1/3. Fresh exact rational differences at epsilon1/100,1/10000,1/1000000 give jump/epsilon=99,9999,999999. Euclidean strategy distance adds constant sqrt2 only. Distinct left/right limits show no tie-only adjustment can make it continuous.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_scope: Local affine behavior in a strict-response region is true but not global Lipschitzness. The zero-sum min-of-linear proof depends on equality of own rewards across best responses, absent here. Simplification and an interior switch do not prevent the jump.
independent_check.severity_and_repair: Major retained for the explicit global theorem and nearby-advantage interpretation. A compatible-boundary assumption or region-restricted statement would change the claim; no replacement global theorem or empirical-failure conclusion is certified.
